trace: Current catalog source declares the vambrace placements in left, right order, with each surface naming its corresponding forearm. The brigandine currently has one chest placement. This describes checked-in source data, not observed runtime output.

The current mirrored-vambrace evidence helper assigns placement index 0 to LeftArm and index 1 to RightArm, independently of the placement ID or its actual protection regions. It indexes directly. The forced-brigandine fixture similarly selects placement 0.

The coverage projector skips regions whose mapped body part differs from the requested part. A hypothetical reversal of the two existing left/right vambrace placement entries would therefore supply the opposite arm region to each mirrored case and produce no matching coverage segments. A hypothetical single-placement input would reach index 1 if this helper were called. These are source-level conditional consequences only: whether such catalog variants are admitted by every applicable validator and policy is not established.

The inspected generic equipment validator checks a nonempty placements array, unique stable IDs and per-placement content. The shown checks do not establish an item-specific left/right position invariant. Other admission rules, generated representations and cross-document validators remain to be traced; absence from these shown ranges is not proof that the complete admission boundary accepts the hypothetical inputs.

The roster projection separately selects a placement by the occurrence order and derives its body parts from the selected placement. The evidence helper is called when constructing the acceptance-evidence object, which the iteration command writes before its matchup summaries. No command, test, parser, simulation or runtime was executed.
first_open_question: Does the complete catalog admission and product policy require exactly these item-specific placement positions, or may placement ordering/count vary? Trace all validators, consumers, and any semantic placement owner before selecting a repair.
repair_direction: If ordering is not an intentional admitted contract, resolve each evidence case by its semantic placement/body-part identity with a documented ambiguity or absence error. If ordering is intentional, make the exact invariant explicit and enforce it at the owning admission boundary. Preserve legitimate multi-placement equipment and report actual projected coverage.
later_acceptance: After separate implementation authorization, verify intended mirrored coverage, reordered entries and absent or ambiguous placements against the chosen contract, and ensure failures are reported at the appropriate boundary.
Reconcile the affected historical roles, other evidence consumers and queue aliases before claiming a connected repair or lens closure.
